practiceQuestions.q: Who was the founder of the Gaekwad dynasty of Baroda?
practiceQuestions.sol: Pilaji Rao Gaekwad founded the Gaekwad dynasty in the early 18th century after establishing Maratha power in Gujarat. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History / Standard Maratha History]

practiceQuestions.q: In which year did the Gaekwads capture the city of Baroda (Vadodara) to make it their capital?
practiceQuestions.sol: Baroda was captured from the Babi rulers in 1734 by Pilaji Rao Gaekwad (or consolidated around this period by Damaji Rao), subsequently becoming the permanent seat of the dynasty. [Primary Reference: Gazetteer of the Baroda State]

practiceQuestions.q: Which Maratha statesman and Peshwa was a contemporary of early Gaekwad rulers and integrated them into the Maratha Confederacy?
practiceQuestions.sol: Baji Rao I played a pivotal role in organizing the Maratha Confederacy, assigning regions of influence in Gujarat to the Gaekwads alongside the Kadam Bahirs. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Who among the following Gaekwad rulers is most renowned for introducing compulsory primary education and radical social reforms in Baroda State?
practiceQuestions.sol: Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III (ruled 1875–1939) introduced free and compulsory primary education in 1906, patronized Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, and enacted major social legislations. [Primary Reference: Indian History & Modern State Reforms Archives]

practiceQuestions.q: In which famous battle of 1761 did the Maratha forces, including contingents from the Gaekwads, suffer a monumental defeat against Ahmad Shah Abdali?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Third Battle of Panipat (1761) involved Maratha armies from across the confederacy fighting against the Afghan invader Ahmad Shah Abdali. [Primary Reference: NCERT Class 12 History]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the primary fiscal right collected by the Gaekwads and other Maratha chiefs from territories outside their direct governance called?
practiceQuestions.sol: Chauth (25% of revenue) and Sardeshmukhi (additional 10%) were the primary revenue-extraction mechanisms employed by Maratha chiefs including the Gaekwads in Gujarat. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India]

practiceQuestions.q: Which British treaty in the early 19th century formally subordinated Baroda State, making it a princely state under British paramountcy?
opts: Treaty of Cambay (1802) / Subsidiary Treaty of Baroda (1805)
practiceQuestions.sol: The Subsidiary Alliance signed between the East India Company and Anand Rao Gaekwad in 1805 established British paramountcy and stationed a British resident in Baroda. [Primary Reference: Aitchison's Treaties, Engagements and Sanads]

practiceQuestions.q: What is the name of the grand palace built by Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III in Baroda, which is one of the largest private dwellings in the world?
practiceQuestions.sol: The Laxmi Vilas Palace was commissioned by Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III in 1890 and designed in the Indo-Saracenic architectural style. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) Cultural Portal]

practiceQuestions.q: Who assassinated Gangadhar Shastri, an envoy of the Peshwa, leading to a major diplomatic and political crisis between the Peshwa and the Gaekwads in 1815?
opts: Trimbakji Dangria (under Malhar Rao/conspiracy involving Gaekwad court factions)
practiceQuestions.sol: The murder of Gangadhar Shastri in Pandharpur in 1815 while he was negotiating revenue disputes between the Peshwa and Gaekwad created immense friction, heavily exploited by the British under Mountstuart Elphinstone. [Primary Reference: Bipan Chandra / Standard Modern Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q: Which financial institution was established by Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III in 1908, which later evolved into the Bank of Baroda?
practiceQuestions.sol: Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III founded the Bank of Baroda on July 20, 1908, along with prominent industrialists like the Scindias and Seth Heerjee, fostering economic development. [Primary Reference: Reserve Bank of India / Bank of Baroda Archives]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the geographic location of Baroda shape the military and administrative strategy of the early Gaekwads under Pilaji Rao and Damaji Rao?
opts: It isolated them from all external conflicts, allowing peaceful maritime trade development only.
Positioned at the crossroads of Malwa, Rajasthan, and the Saurashtra peninsula, it required balancing Mughal remnants, local Rajput chiefs, and rival Maratha clans like the Holkars and Scindias.
It restricted their expansion strictly to the southern Deccan plateau under the direct orders of Pune.
It forced them to abandon cavalry warfare in favor of navy-exclusive operations in the Arabian Sea.
practiceQuestions.sol: Baroda's strategic location in Gujarat acted as a gateway to wealthy coastal trade routes and rich agricultural plains, while placing the Gaekwads at the center of multi-polar geopolitical friction involving Mughals, the Peshwa, and regional satraps. [Primary Reference: NCERT Themes in Indian History / Satish Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the structural nature of the financial settlements between the Peshwa at Pune and the Gaekwad of Baroda regarding Gujarat's revenues?
opts: Complete financial autonomy with zero remittance obligations to Pune.
A dual-sharing system of revenue collection (half-share/partition of chauth and territories), often leading to intense fiscal negotiations, military interventions, and debt accumulation.
Direct taxation collected by British auditors stationed in Pune on behalf of Baroda.
A fixed annual religious tax paid directly to temple trusts in Gujarat without state mediation.
practiceQuestions.sol: The fiscal framework between the Peshwa and Damaji Rao Gaekwad involved sharing the revenues of Gujarat equally (half-share), which required complex revenue-farming and military backing, frequently mediated or capitalized upon by British agents. [Primary Reference: Maratha Confederacy Administration Records]

practiceQuestions.q: How did Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III's administrative policies reflect a synthesis of progressive modernization and native state autonomy?
opts: By rejecting all Western educational models and strictly enforcing 17th-century feudal customs.
By instituting universal primary education, judicial separation of powers, local self-government, and economic investments while navigating British paramountcy.
By dissolving the state apparatus and voluntarily handing over all administration to the Viceroy's council.
By focusing exclusively on building military stockpiles to wage an open war against the British Raj.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sayaji Rao III transformed Baroda into one of the most progressive princely states by introducing judicial reforms, compulsory education, library networks, and social upliftment, balancing internal reform with the constraints of British paramountcy. [Primary Reference: Princely India State Reports / Baroda Administration]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the significance of the trial of Malhar Rao Gaekwad in 1875 by the British colonial administration?
opts: It marked the absolute withdrawal of British interference in Baroda's internal affairs.
It was a landmark assertion of British paramountcy where a Maharaja was charged with attempting to poison the British resident, leading to his deposition.
It resulted in Malhar Rao being promoted to the head of the Maratha Confederacy.
It led to the complete annexation of Baroda directly into the Bombay Presidency without a native successor.
practiceQuestions.sol: Malhar Rao was tried by a special mixed commission of British and Indian nobles in 1875 on charges of attempting to poison Colonel Robert Phayre. Though the commission was divided, the British deposed him for 'notorious misrule', opening the way for the adoption of Sayaji Rao III. [Primary Reference: Imperial Gazetteer of India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Gaekwads manage their relations with the Bhil and Koli tribal populations in the forest and border tracts of Gujarat?
opts: Through total annihilation and displacement from the region.
Through a mix of punitive military expeditions, employment as irregular watchmen/soldiery (grassias/sebandis), and negotiated tribute settlements to secure trade routes.
By granting them absolute sovereign independence over all urban centres of Baroda.
By completely ignoring their presence and outsourcing revenue collection to Portuguese traders.
practiceQuestions.sol: Tribal groups like the Bhils and Kolis posed both a challenge and a resource; early Gaekwad rulers engaged in a pragmatic policy of pacification, using force when necessary but also incorporating them into local security frameworks. [Primary Reference: Gujarat District Gazetteers]

practiceQuestions.q: In the context of the Maratha Confederacy's institutional structure, what distinguished the Gaekwads from autonomous entities like the Holkars, Scindias, and Bhonsles?
opts: Their geographical focus on Gujarat and Western coastal plains, combined with shared revenue-splitting arrangements with the Peshwa.
They never acknowledged the authority of the Peshwa under any circumstances.
They operated exclusively as a naval power in the Bay of Bengal.
They converted Baroda into a British-administered province as early as 1750.
practiceQuestions.sol: While Scindias controlled Gwalior/Central India, Holkars controlled Indore, and Bhonsles controlled Nagpur, the Gaekwads carved out their sphere in Gujarat, characterized by deep integration with the financial hubs of Western India and specific revenue-sharing compacts with Pune. [Primary Reference: NCERT History / Modern Indian History Canon]

practiceQuestions.q: What role did economic diversification and agricultural experimentation play during the reign of Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III?
opts: It caused widespread agrarian distress and famine due to heavy taxation on tobacco and cotton.
It promoted scientific agriculture, experimental farms, cotton mills, dairy farming, and railway expansion, establishing Baroda as an industrializing princely state.
It was completely abandoned in favor of importing all food grains from Britain.
It restricted economic activity exclusively to traditional handloom weaving.
practiceQuestions.sol: Sayaji Rao III invested heavily in infrastructure, agricultural research, technical education, and railways (Gaekwad's Baroda State Railway), transforming the state's economy. [Primary Reference: Baroda Economic Surveys / Economic History of India]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the Gaekwads interact with European trading companies (such as the British and Portuguese) operating along the Gujarat coastline?
opts: By maintaining complete isolation and banning all foreign ships from entering Gujarat ports.
Through a pragmatic mix of customs duties negotiation, commercial agreements, and military alliances to check rival local powers and secure artillery supplies.
By surrendering all sovereign tax rights to the Portuguese governor in Goa.
By acting as naval mercenaries for the French East India Company exclusively.
practiceQuestions.sol: The Gaekwads pragmatically engaged with European powers like the British and Portuguese, balancing commercial interests, port revenues, and military logistics before the Subsidiary Alliance locked Baroda into the British sphere. [Primary Reference: British-Maratha Diplomatic Archives]

practiceQuestions.q: What was the administrative impact of the 'Gaikwad Contingent' clause under the Subsidiary Alliance of 1805?
opts: It required the Gaekwad to maintain a permanent British-officered subsidiary force funded by assigned revenues, which strained the state treasury.
It dissolved the native army and replaced it with a volunteer militia chosen by democratic elections.
It required the British to pay a monthly tribute directly to the Gaekwad court.
It prohibited the Gaekwad from maintaining any armed personnel whatsoever.
practiceQuestions.sol: The subsidiary treaty mandated the maintenance of a British auxiliary force at Baroda's expense, which heavily burdened state finances and increased British political leverage over internal administration. [Primary Reference: Aitchison's Treaties / Princely States Studies]

practiceQuestions.q: How did the cultural patronage of the Gaekwads contribute to the development of Indian art and music?
opts: They prohibited classical music and painting in favor of religious orthodoxy.
They patronized legendary classical musicians (such as Ustad Moula Bux, Faiyaz Khan), Sanskrit scholars, and painters (like Raja Ravi Varma), turning Baroda into a vibrant cultural capital.
They exclusively funded Western opera houses while destroying indigenous Indian art forms.
They maintained a strict ban on all visual arts, allowing only architectural construction of military forts.
practiceQuestions.sol: Baroda under the Gaekwads, particularly Sayaji Rao III, became a renowned patron of arts and music, establishing the Baroda State School of Music and commissioning works from master artists like Raja Ravi Varma. [Primary Reference: NCERT An Introduction to Indian Art]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the origin and early expansion of the Gaekwad dynasty:
1. Pilaji Rao Gaekwad started his career as a military commander under Dabhade, the Maratha Senapati of Gujarat.
2. The Gaekwads successfully established their permanent capital at Baroda in the early 18th century after defeating the Mughal provincial governors and local rulers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are historically accurate. Pilaji Rao rose through the ranks serving the Dabhade family (the Maratha commanders holding authority in Gujarat), and subsequently consolidated Baroda as the dynastic capital by overcoming Mughal and local opposition. [Primary Reference: Satish Chandra, Medieval India / Standard History Textbooks]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about Damaji Rao Gaekwad:
1. He played a crucial role in expanding Maratha influence across Gujarat and parts of Kathiawar.
2. He remained completely independent of the Peshwa's authority throughout his life and never participated in pan-Maratha confederacy wars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Damaji Rao expanded Maratha sway across Gujarat and Kathiawar. Statement 2 is incorrect because Damaji Rao was subdued and reconciled by Peshwa Balaji Baji Rao in 1752, resulting in a formal revenue-sharing and military obligation agreement, and he also participated in pan-Maratha campaigns like Panipat (1761). [Primary Reference: Maratha Historical Records]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III:
1. He was originally named Gopal Rao and was adopted into the Gaekwad family from a collateral branch.
2. He enacted legislation banning child marriage and caste-based discrimination within Baroda State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. Gopal Rao (born 1863) was selected from a remote branch and adopted by Maharani Jamnabai following the deposition of Malhar Rao, taking the royal name Sayaji Rao III. He was a pioneer of social reform, passing progressive laws against child marriage and untouchability. [Primary Reference: Baroda State Administration Reports / Biographical Archives]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Subsidiary Alliance of Baroda (1805):
1. It was signed between the East India Company and Anand Rao Gaekwad.
2. It permanently abolished the collection of Chauth by the Gaekwads from the territories of Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: The Subsidiary Treaty of 1805 was concluded between the EIC and Anand Rao. Statement 2 is incorrect because the treaty actually reorganized revenue extraction and guaranteed the Gaekwad's share of revenues (including traditional dues) under British protection, rather than abolishing Chauth entirely right at that moment—though Maratha revenue rights were progressively absorbed or settled by the British over subsequent decades. [Primary Reference: Aitchison's Treaties / British-Indian History]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the relations between the Gaekwads and the Peshwa:
1. The Gaekwads were originally subordinates to the Peshwa as members of the Maratha Confederacy.
2. After the Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-1818) and the elimination of the Peshwaship, the Gaekwads' treaties were directly mediated with the British East India Company.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are correct. The Gaekwads were part of the Maratha Confederacy under the supreme executive authority of the Peshwa. Following the collapse of the Maratha Empire in 1818, the British dealt with the princely states directly, removing the Peshwa's mediation over Baroda's tribute. [Primary Reference: Modern Indian History / Bipan Chandra]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cultural and educational contributions of Baroda State under the Gaekwads:
1. Baroda was among the first princely states to establish a network of free public libraries across villages and towns.
2. Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III provided financial assistance and scholarship to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar for his higher education abroad.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are accurate. Sayaji Rao III pioneered a unique public library movement across Baroda state with the help of American librarian W.A. Borden, and he famously supported Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's studies at Columbia University. [Primary Reference: Cultural Archives of Baroda State / Historical Biographies]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the economic reforms of Baroda State:
1. The Bank of Baroda was founded in 1908 under the patronage of Maharaja Sayaji Rao Gaekwad III.
2. Baroda State strictly prohibited industrialization and factory labor laws to preserve traditional agrarian structures.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Bank of Baroda was established in 1908 by the Gaekwad. Statement 2 is incorrect because Baroda actively promoted industrialization, textile mills, and modern economic enterprises, rather than prohibiting them. [Primary Reference: Economic History of Baroda State]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the architectural legacy of the Gaekwads:
1. The Laxmi Vilas Palace in Baroda was designed in the Indo-Saracenic architectural style and constructed during the reign of Sayaji Rao III.
2. The Gaekwads completely avoided Western architectural influences, relying solely on ancient Maratha temple styles.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Laxmi Vilas Palace is a prime example of Indo-Saracenic architecture built under Sayaji Rao III. Statement 2 is incorrect because Baroda's public and royal architecture prominently blended European (Gothic, Renaissance) and indigenous Indian motifs. [Primary Reference: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the geopolitical position of Baroda State under British paramountcy:
1. Baroda was categorized as a 'Salute State', receiving a 21-gun salute, which placed it among the highest-ranking princely states in the British Indian Empire.
2. The British resident stationed at Baroda had zero interference in the internal judicial and financial administration of the state throughout the 19th and 20th centuries.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Baroda was one of the five premier princely states entitled to a 21-gun salute. Statement 2 is incorrect because British residents and the Governor-General's agents frequently intervened in Baroda's internal affairs, notably during the trial of Malhar Rao Gaekwad and through political surveillance over Sayaji Rao III. [Primary Reference: Imperial Gazetteer of India / Princely States Archives]

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the integration of Baroda State into the Indian Union post-independence:
1. Baroda was the very first princely state in Gujarat to sign the Instrument of Accession, facilitated by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and V.P. Menon.
2. Maharaja Pratapsinh Rao Gaekwad signed the merger agreement, and Baroda was subsequently integrated into the Bombay State.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because Nilambag / Bhavnagar or other smaller states were among the very first in the region, while Baroda signed later in 1948. Statement 2 is correct: Maharaja Pratapsinh Rao Gaekwad signed the merger agreement, leading to the incorporation of Baroda into the Bombay State prior to the formation of Gujarat state in 1960. [Primary Reference: V.P. Menon, 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States']
